Nu Holdings Soars 11% on Record $1.1 Billion Profit as It Takes "First Steps Beyond Latin America" ©@Juan Moyano via Canva, @kanchanachitkhamma via Canva
Key Takeaways

Nu Holdings shares jumped 11% today on record third-quarter net income of $1.1 billion.

Nu is deliberately taking on more credit risk, and its 32% return on equity pays for it.

Nu's loans grew far faster than Itaú Unibanco's and Bradesco's, and it now takes on MercadoLibre in Mexico.

Before today's jump, the stock traded at 4.4x tangible book value, about half its three-year average.

Nu Holdings (NU:NYSE) stock is up 11% today after it reported record third-quarter net income of $1.1 billion, up 31% FX-neutral, after Thursday's close. Founder and CEO David Vélez said the quarter included Nu's "first steps beyond Latin America."

At home, Nu's credit portfolio grew 33% over the year to $41.6 billion, far faster than loans to individuals at Itaú Unibanco (ITUB), up 9.6%, and Banco Bradesco (BBD), up 7.4%. And in Mexico, where Nu just finished its first quarter as a full bank, it goes up against MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ).

TIKR tracks 23 analysts on Nu Holdings. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Nu Holdings, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Nu Holdings' Analyst Ratings

More profit, and more risk by design

Return on equity hit 32%, but the 90+ day NPL ratio rose to 7.3% from 6.9% in the second quarter.

That's on purpose. "We continue to expand our credit portfolio, deliberately taking some additional risk when the expected returns justify it," CFO Rob Livingston said on the call. Excluding one-off items, Nu's risk-adjusted net interest margin rose to 12.7% from 11.9% in the second quarter.

Itaú's 90-day NPL ratio was 2.0%, barely above 1.9% a year earlier, so the rise in Nu's bad loans looks like Nu's own choice. And Nu's ROE beats Itaú's 23.6%.

Mexico is the next test, where Nu now has 16.6 million customers. MercadoLibre says it gained fintech share there in its own third quarter, but its operating income fell 6% as it reinvested. Can it keep pushing against a full-fledged Nu bank while already giving up margin?

Cheap for a bank growing this fast

Nu also cut its full-year efficiency-ratio forecast to 19%-19.5%, from about 20%.

Analysts expected Nu's normalized EPS to keep climbing well before this report:

Nu Holdings (NU): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

A record quarter and a lower expense forecast give analysts no reason to cut those numbers.

Still, the stock traded at 4.4x tangible book value at the last close. That's the low of its last three years and about half its 8.2x average:

title: Airbnb vs. MercadoLibre: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
detail:
Airbnb vs. MercadoLibre: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
Brendan Coffey, The Motley Fool
Wed, November 11, 2026 at 3:20 PM PST 7 min read
ABNB
MELI
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Choosing between a global travel leader and a Latin American commerce giant requires balancing high growth against established profitability. Which path is right for your portfolio between Airbnb Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) and MercadoLibre Inc. (NASDAQ:MELI)?

Airbnb provides a unique global platform for alternative accommodations, while MercadoLibre operates an expansive ecosystem of e-commerce, fintech, and logistics services across Latin America. Both companies benefit from the digital shift in consumer spending, but they navigate very different competitive landscapes and regional economic conditions as they head toward 2027.

The case for Airbnb

Airbnb connects over 5 million hosts with guests seeking unique stays and experiences in over 220 countries, as detailed in its latest annual report for FY 2025. Its two-sided platform offers hosts tools like integrated payments and protection through AirCover, while providing guests with AI-powered search and personalization features. By maintaining a marketplace rather than owning properties, the company stays lean while expanding its presence among travel and tourism stocks.

In FY 2025, revenue reached about $12.3 billion, representing growth of approximately 10.8% compared to the previous year. The company reported net income of about $2.5 billion for the period. While revenue continued to climb, the net margin of roughly 20.4% was lower than in previous years as the company invested in platform updates and marketing.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.3x, indicating a conservative amount of total debt relative to shareholder equity. The current ratio, measuring the ability to cover short-term liabilities, is roughly 1.4x. In FY 2025, free cash flow reached around $4.6 billion, though stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 34.3% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation.

The case for MercadoLibre

MercadoLibre operates a massive ecosystem in Latin America, which the company detailed in its latest annual report for FY 2025. It integrates a marketplace for buyers and sellers with its Mercado Pago fintech solution and a proprietary logistics network, Mercado Envios, to ensure fast delivery. This integrated approach creates a powerful flywheel where commerce, payments, and logistics reinforce one another for its 136 million unique buyers.

In FY 2025, revenue reached around $28.9 billion, a significant increase of approximately 39.1% compared to the prior year. The company reported net income of roughly $2.0 billion for the same period. While the top line grew rapidly, the net margin was approximately 6.9% as the company focused on market share expansion and its credit business.

Famed investor Michael Burry said on Wednesday that he bought back into apparel maker Lululemon Athletica (LULU) after shares fell into the $106 range, framing the move as a bet on temporary neglect rather than permanent damage.

Re-Entry Into Lululemon

Burry cited new management's failure to reverse a prolonged "black hole" in marketing and messaging, which has left the stock overlooked during a low-information stretch. He expressed confidence in the company's research and product development, calling the current price a favorable risk-reward with limited downside and reiterating his June analysis on the stock.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

In a June Substack piece, the hedge fund manager cataloged a history of self-inflicted setbacks at Lululemon due to bad management, and argued that these episodes create value opportunities, while maintaining that the underlying business is not collapsing but is simply stalled. In early October, he sold shares for a tax loss, temporarily swapping into Deckers Outdoor as a proxy with the explicit intention of repurchasing after the wash-sale window.

Lululemon is currently navigating a dual challenge of sharp earnings pressure and a major leadership overhaul. In its second-quarter fiscal 2026 results, revenue fell 4% to $2.4 billion with comparable sales down 9%, while signature leggings sales plunged about 20%. The company cut full-year guidance to a 5–7% revenue decline and EPS of $9.48–$9.73, well below the prior year's $13.26, and warned of a further 10–11% revenue drop in the third quarter.

New CEO Heidi O'Neill, a longtime Nike executive who took the helm in early September, has rapidly restructured the senior team, appointing a new President & Chief Product Officer, Chief Operating Officer, Chief Brand Officer, and Chief Strategy Officer, aiming to refocus the company on product innovation, brand, and execution.

Burry's Other Portfolio Additions

Burry also increased positions in several other names. He bought more MercadoLibre (MELI) shares below $1,500.

"The falling Brazilian real hurts the company's bottom line. It does help to some extent with international competition from Temu, Shein, and Amazon, but not enough. This is why the stock is down, but it has been punished too harshly," Burry said.

MercadoLibre Stock Fell 20% in a Month After Hitting a New 52-Week Low. Is the Selling Overdone? ©@small smiles from Getty Images via Canva, @anyaberkut from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

MercadoLibre (MELI) stock fell approximately 20% from October 5 to November 10, closing at $1,490.24 after reaching a new 52-week low on November 5.

MercadoLibre's third-quarter revenue and financial income rose 45% to $10.75 billion, but operating margin declined to 6.3% as shipping, fulfillment, and marketing investments pressured profitability.

Sea Limited (SE) reported 41.3% revenue growth at Shopee in the third quarter, while Nu Holdings (NU) provides another perspective on Brazilian consumer credit conditions.

MercadoLibre appears potentially undervalued following the selloff, although stronger margins and continued market share gains will be important to a sustained recovery.

What Happened?

MercadoLibre (MELI) stock declined approximately 20% from its October 5 closing price of $1,860.61 to $1,490.24 on November 10, after hitting a new 52-week low on November 5.

The decline reflects two concerns: political uncertainty in Brazil and weaker-than-expected profitability despite strong revenue growth.

Brazil's October 25 presidential runoff delivered another term for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who defeated Flávio Bolsonaro after trailing him in the first round.

MercadoLibre shares fell approximately 8% on October 26 as investors reassessed Brazil's economic outlook, currency risks, and consumer spending conditions.

Brazil generated approximately $15.2 billion of MercadoLibre's $28.9 billion in 2025 revenue, making it the company's largest market.

However, the company's third-quarter earnings report created a more immediate concern.

According to MercadoLibre's third-quarter financial results, revenue and financial income increased 45% year over year to $10.75 billion, but reported earnings of $8.83 per share fell short of the $9.27 consensus estimate cited in the initial research brief.

Operating margin declined to 6.3% from approximately 9.8% a year earlier, reflecting higher shipping expenses, expanded fulfillment capacity, and increased marketing spending in Brazil.

In its third-quarter shareholder letter, management described the pressure on shipping margins as "the price of the habit we set out to build."

The strategy is producing results. Items sold in Brazil increased more than 40% year over year for the fifth consecutive quarter, while MercadoLibre gained market share across its three largest markets.

Its lower free-shipping threshold also encouraged smaller purchases, initially putting pressure on shipping economics.

By September, Brazilian orders valued between R$19 and R$79 that qualified for free or slower delivery became variable contribution-positive for the first time, suggesting higher order volumes are beginning to improve shipping economics.

MercadoLibre operates one of Latin America's largest e-commerce and financial technology platforms. It generates revenue through online shopping, digital payments, advertising, lending and logistics services.

In a November 10 Substack post, Burry acknowledged Nvidia's short-term recovery potential while expressing doubts about its longer-term investment appeal.

"I am not tempted as a long-term hold from here, but I imagine the whole market is going to think this is a heck of a trade fairly soon," Burry said.

His concern centers on whether Nvidia can maintain its technological dominance over the next five years as competition intensifies.

Meanwhile, Burry identified MercadoLibre and Australian online furniture retailer Temple & Webster as his two largest positions, each representing more than 10% of his portfolio.

He disclosed purchasing additional MercadoLibre shares twice below $1,500 and indicated he would consider buying more following another 20% decline.

Burry also added to Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE), JD.com (NASDAQ:JD) and long-dated Sprouts Farmers Market (NASDAQ:SFM) call options.

Investors Takeaway

Nvidia's November 17 earnings report represents an immediate test of Burry's cautious outlook.

Investors should monitor AI accelerator demand, gross margins and competition from custom chips developed by major cloud providers.

For MercadoLibre, the critical question is whether strong e-commerce and payments growth can translate into improving profitability.

Investors should track operating margins, logistics expenses and Mercado Pago credit performance.

Burry's positioning suggests a preference for established businesses trading at more attractive valuations rather than relying exclusively on AI enthusiasm.

However, his disclosed purchases are not guarantees of future returns, and further margin compression could weaken MercadoLibre's investment case.
